corpus.note: Outcomes are inferred from transcript language, not CRM-verified.

rules.note: Ingestion and normalisation rules. These are policy, not inference — every one was decided by the client and is applied uniformly across the corpus. Anything the rules cannot settle is surfaced on the dashboard rather than guessed at silently.

speaker_resolution.detail: Fathom tags the closer with a '(Primal Instinct)' suffix on their speaker label. That label identifies the rep. Every other speaker label in the transcript collapses to a single 'prospect' role.
handles: Diarization swapping speakers on short turns — role is assigned per label, not per line, so a swap misattributes a line but never invents a third participant
A prospect changing device mid-call and acquiring a new label (e.g. 'Francisco Adain Vega' becoming "Paco's iPhone 17") — both labels collapse to the same prospect role
speaker_resolution.known_limit: Because diarization genuinely swaps lines, per-line attribution stays approximate. Talk-ratio and who-raised-the-objection metrics are therefore NOT published. Role-level facts (an objection occurred, a phase was run) are safe; line-level ones are not.
speaker_resolution.multi_rep_calls: If more than one '(Primal Instinct)' label appears, the rep with the most speaking turns is the closer; the rest are logged as additional_reps.

prospect_identity.detail: Prospect name is taken from the file title where present ('Name x Rep'). For untitled files ('Impromptu Zoom Meeting') it is recovered from the first non-rep speaker label in the transcript.
prospect_identity.normalisation: Lowercased, punctuation and device suffixes stripped, whitespace collapsed. Used as the deal key.

deal_merging.detail: Multiple calls with the same canonical prospect are a single deal. The deal carries the outcome of its LAST call chronologically, since that is the furthest the conversation actually got.
deal_merging.rationale: Counting calls as deals double-counts prospects and understates close rate. The unit that matters commercially is the deal.
deal_merging.cash: Deal cash is taken from the closing call only, never summed across calls in the sequence.
deal_merging.adherence: Adherence stays scored per call. A discovery call and a follow-up call are judged against different parts of the script, so averaging them would hide which part failed.

junk_filter.detail: Transcripts below 2 KB are failed or aborted recordings — connection drops, no-shows, empty rooms. Observed examples in the corpus run from 96 bytes to roughly 1.2 KB.
junk_filter.reporting: Excluded files are counted and reported, never silently dropped. A rising junk count is itself a signal about recording setup.

close_rule.detail: A verbal agreement to move forward plus a payment link sent counts as CLOSED, even where the transcript ends before payment confirms.
close_rule.known_bias: Overstates close rate against any deal that agreed and then never paid. Joining a payments export would quantify the gap.
close_rule.cash_treatment: Where a payment plan was agreed, cash is recorded as contract value with the instalment terms retained separately, so cash-collected and contract-value can be reported apart.

instances.detail: Isolated correctly ('outside of the investment, ready to draw a line in the sand?'), then ran the financial picture: cash on hand $1,500, monthly leftover $800, savings yes, credit score 650. Missed the credit-card depth the script calls for — number of cards, available credit per card, used vs available — and never asked about crypto, stocks or investments. Still structured $1,200 x 6 live and got a yes.

Opened the door correctly — 'my intention is to never take food off people's tables. If there's a way we can structure this, are you open to exploring that?' → got a YES. Then never ran the financial picture. Not one question about cash on hand, monthly surplus, credit or assets. The play was started and abandoned.

The money objection landed and no part of the play ran. No isolate, no 'should I vs how' reframe, no offer to structure it, no financial picture. Instead the rep ran a takeaway — 'go back to her' — twice. A takeaway is not in the script.

The rep used a partial-value reframe and a good path-to-yes question ('what would be the route to getting you back to swinging stuff around?'), but ran none of the scripted OE moves: no certainty question, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before.

P1.evidence: 'Where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can show you the options.' Three-part rather than four-part, but framed and agreed. Setter Kim's notes not read back despite a pre-qualified handoff.

adherence.notes: The most expensive miss in the pilot. A high-intent prospect who explicitly said the price made him MORE interested, met two scripted objections back to back, and neither play was run. The rep also hit a hard calendar stop mid-objection.

source.display_title: 07/23/2026 - Robyn Stillwater x  Andrew Musial — Closed

setter.evidence: No setter code in title. Referral came via her partner Tyler, an existing client.

prospect.name: Robyn Stillwater
prospect.location: Emigration Canyon / Salt Lake City, Utah, USA
prospect.family_status: Partnered with Tyler (existing Primal client); planning pregnancy from August 2026
prospect.training_background: Bodyweight work, reverse treadmill for knees. Mirroring partner's program. Not structured.

signals: Partner Tyler already enrolled and visibly progressing — social proof arrived pre-call
Price was pre-framed by the partner before the call ever happened
Zero price objection raised at any point
Explicitly wants her own individualized journey, not a copy of her partner's
Closed same-call, live on the payment link

goals.text: More stability and balance, to carry into old age
Rebuild confidence in a previously dislocated shoulder
Be fit through pregnancy and strong postpartum
Become a better dancer — jazz, somatic, swing, tango
Do more hiking and backpacking
Have physical confidence spread to other parts of life

pains.text: Scoliosis (13 degrees) causing lower back and sciatic strain
Left shoulder dislocated 5 years ago, undiagnosed for a period; 18-month recovery
Tendonitis in both knees since age 18; ongoing strength issues
History of depression driving a sedentary period
Late-night eating rooted in childhood safety patterns; disrupts sleep
Night owl; struggles to sleep before midnight
Gyms are overwhelming — 'I turn around and walk out'
Doesn't know if she's performing movements correctly; fears self-injury

objections.raw_quote: Tyler and I are planning on trying to get pregnant soon. And so I realized that that is going to affect the program.
objections.rep_response: We are in a perfect place — coming in strong and healthy makes postpartum recovery far easier. Also confirmed the subscription can be paused for pregnancy or injury.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: Six months, full transformation guarantee; program can be paused for pregnancy or injury

evidence: Payment link sent in Zoom chat during the call
Prospect: 'Looks like it just went through' — rep confirms: 'Yes, yes, that went through'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked live for Monday 11:15 MT
WhatsApp numbers exchanged; onboarding form and agreement promised
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor, Monday 11:15 MT

notable.note: The only call of the five where price was never contested. The partner had already covered the investment before the call. Objection handling was spent entirely on a life-event concern, not money.

quality.notes: Speaker labels swap on short turns throughout; one long run around 00:03:51-00:05:00 is attributed almost entirely to the wrong speaker. Long-form content is attributable by voice/context.

P1.evidence: Warm, rapport-led open — 'what got you interested in doing this too?' No four-part frame, no frame agreement, no notes read back.

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the pilot. Height 5'5", weight 144, work status, scoliosis, shoulder dislocation, knee tendonitis, depression history, full nutrition and intermittent-fasting detail, extended sleep discussion. Never asked age.

P3.evidence: 'If you could change one thing about how you feel or move?' → stability and balance → 'spread to other parts of my life' → probed that → confidence → dancing, hiking, pregnancy, old age. Clean reflect-back: 'this goes much further than only losing extra pounds.'

P4.evidence: The prospect volunteered the root cause unprompted — 'whenever I've gone and done any other programs, I don't even know if I'm doing this right.' The rep never asked what she had tried, what happened, or why it didn't stick. Phase effectively skipped.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame at any point. Cost of inaction never made real.

P6.evidence: 'If you had everything that you needed, do you feel genuinely that you're going to get to your goals?' → 'Yes.' → 'No hesitation.' Clean verbal yes before presenting.

P11.evidence: Payment confirmed live — 'that went through.' Trevor call booked Monday 11:15 MT. Agreement was promised for later by email rather than signed on the call. Onboarding form mentioned as a follow-up; no Skool link or welcome-email instruction given.

objection_plays.detail: No money, timing, spouse, think-about-it or fear objection was ever raised. The only concern was a pregnancy plan, handled with a reframe plus the pause guarantee. This is what a pre-framed warm referral looks like.

adherence.notes: Closed on the strength of discovery and a warm referral despite skipping phases 4 and 5 entirely. Demonstrates that a pre-sold prospect masks script gaps — which is exactly why close rate alone is a poor coaching signal.

source.display_title: 07/30/2026 - Impromptu Zoom Meeting (Francisco Adain Vega) — Closed (unconfirmed)

setter.evidence: Inbound: prospect saw Trevor's content and booked directly. 'you guys popped up yesterday as I was browsing'

prospect.name: Francisco Adain Vega
prospect.training_background: Former basketball and soccer player; on-and-off gym. Dislikes gyms, prefers home training.
prospect.medical: Thyroid treatment ~9 months, causing significant weight gain; ends approx August 2026. Knee surgery 15 years ago.

signals: Health setback (thyroid treatment) caused the decline, not neglect
Explicit desire to get back to a former self rather than reach a new peak
Visible regret framing: 'I wish I could have started sooner'
Cyclical on/off history with training; names motivation as the blocker
Constrained budget — needed a payment plan to proceed

goals.text: Lose 20-30 lb, from 228 down to ~200
Regain flexibility lost with age
Build endurance; stop tiring quickly
Return to competitive basketball and soccer leagues
Build consistency and break the on-off cycle
Model confidence and follow-through for his 15-year-old daughter

pains.text: Knee pain and stiffness on waking; prior knee surgery
Lower back pain on the right, on and off through the day, from weight compensation
Thyroid treatment drove weight gain outside his control
Cannot sustain consistency — good for 2 weeks, then slacks for 2-3
Dislikes the gym; lacks home equipment
Training feels like an obligation, not something he wants to do
Poor snacking — cookies, chips, several times a week
Regret about not starting sooner; audibly deflated when describing his future self

objections.raw_quote: It's a little over the budget that I thought, but yeah, we can look into it.
objections.rep_response: Isolated the objection ('do you mean you just don't have it available at the moment?'), confirmed commitment outside of price, then ran a resources qualification: available now, monthly surplus, savings, credit score.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I don't have it available at the moment, honestly.
objections.rep_response: Structured a live payment plan: $1,200 x 6 months, with the option to accelerate if more becomes available.

objections.raw_quote: I'm not done. I see the doctor in two weeks, and I'm hoping there I'll be done with the treatment.
objections.rep_response: Do you feel like you are able to already begin with the training and the mobility, even though it's still finishing up?

evidence: Payment plan agreed: rep says 'Let's get you rolling with that' — prospect: 'Yeah'
Payment link sent during the call and receipt acknowledged — 'yeah, yeah, it's just my internet's a little slow right now'
Onboarding with Trevor set for Monday 4:15pm ET
Transcript ends before an explicit payment confirmation, but under the agreed close rule verbal agreement plus link sent counts as closed
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor, Monday 16:15 ET

notable.note: Closed under the agreed rule rather than by an explicit in-transcript payment confirmation. Cash is booked as the payment-plan total ($1,200 x 6 = $7,200), which is contract value, not cash collected on the day — the first instalment is $1,200.

quality.notes: SEVERE. Speaker labels invert repeatedly — many of the rep's discovery questions are attributed to the prospect and vice versa. Additionally the prospect's label changes mid-call from 'Francisco Adain Vega' to 'Paco's iPhone 17' when he rejoined from his phone, so a naive parser would count him as two people. All extraction here was done by reading role from content, not from labels.

P1.evidence: Set a fit-or-refer frame — 'if we really fit in there, let's get you started. If not, point you in the best direction. Sounds good?' — and got agreement. Not the scripted four-part frame. Referenced the application but did not read notes back.

P2.evidence: Weight 228, age 47, height 5'10". Thyroid treatment and prior knee surgery captured. Full day-of-eating walkthrough. Missed occupation, sleep entirely, and results-from-current-training.

P3.evidence: Drove from weight loss through endurance to playing competitive basketball, then to confidence, then to modelling follow-through for his 15-year-old daughter. Hit the family/identity layer the script demands. Did not do a clean 'so this isn't really about the weight' reflect-back.

P4.evidence: 'What do you feel is stopping you from committing to something completely?' → 'not finding the right training, and motivating myself.' Then challenged it: 'Do you think trying to motivate yourself is always going to help you stick to something?'

P5.evidence: Textbook. 'Six months from now, 12 months from now, you're still in the same position... do you feel like that's something you can settle for?' → 'No. I can't settle for that. That's just not what I want.' The only full consequence frame in the pilot.

P6.evidence: Ran the commitment gate twice before price — 'is there anything that would stop you from being able to 100% commit?' → 'No, not that I can think of.' Then again after the pillars. Only presented the 6K after a clear yes.

P11.evidence: Payment link sent but the call cuts to voicemail before confirmation. Trevor call set for Monday 4:15pm ET. No agreement signed on the call. No welcome email, Skool link or onboarding questionnaire instruction.

objection_plays.detail: Isolated correctly ('outside of the investment, ready to draw a line in the sand?'), then ran the financial picture: cash on hand $1,500, monthly leftover $800, savings yes, credit score 650. Missed the credit-card depth the script calls for — number of cards, available credit per card, used vs available — and never asked about crypto, stocks or investments. Still structured $1,200 x 6 live and got a yes.

adherence.notes: Highest adherence in the pilot and the most complete objection handling. Also the call the script's own phase 11 failed hardest — steps 3 and 4 never happened, which is exactly why the close cannot be confirmed.
